summary: Geshe Tashi Tsering works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1970–1987), Gyuto Monastery (~1987–1988), and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He taught at Kopan Monastery (~1988–1992) and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (1994).

Geshe Tenzin Dhargye is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, Gyume Tantric College, and under Ling Rinpoche. He held teaching posts at Sera, Gyume, and the University of Virginia (1999–2000).
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned Geshe degrees studying at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery, and he taught Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

Geshe Wangyal was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Agvan Dorzhiev (~1921–1937) and at Drepung Monastery (~1923–1938). He later taught at Columbia University (~1962–1972) and the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983).

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991, 2004, and as a scholar from 2014 to 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1939–1959) and under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at CIHTS (~1968–1970).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University, where he later served as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gheorghe Bogdan-Duică was an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Jena, the University of Vienna, and the University of Bucharest. In 1919, he became Professor of Modern Romanian Literature at Babeș-Bolyai University.

Gherardo De Vincentiis worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as linguistics. He studied under Giacomo Lignana and served as an incaricato at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" in 1878.

Gherardo Gnoli specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Antonino Pagliaro, later holding professorships at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008).

Ghulam Yazdani worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Aligarh Muslim University under C. F. Andrews, Mohammad Ishaq, and Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi, he taught at St. Stephen's College, Rajshahi College, and Government College University before directing Hyderabad's archaeology department (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Raniero Gnoli at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and at Sapienza University of Rome, later serving as Associate Professor at "L'Orientale" (1998–2017).

Giacomo Devoto was a linguist who studied at Pavia, Berlin, Basel, and Paris under scholars including Luigi Suali, Antoine Meillet, and Jacob Wackernagel. He held professorships at Cagliari (1927), Florence (1928, 1939), and Padua (1930).

Giacomo Lignana worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Turin and under Christian Lassen and Friedrich von Spiegel. He held professorships at Naples Federico II (1860–1870), Bologna (~1861–1862), and Sapienza University of Rome (1870).
Gianpaolo Vetturini works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of London, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1911–1914). He served on the faculty at Kyoto University (1929; 1935–1948), Rissho University (~1924), and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya and later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned his degrees at Kyoto University studying under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1968–1972) and Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998), studying under Carl Bielefeldt, Bernard Faure, and others. He held teaching posts at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and Insight Meditation Center (~2001).
